BARIN GHOSH, C. J. (Oral)
 There has been some delay in preferring these appeals.
Accordingly, Applications for condonation of delay have been filed. No
objection thereto have been filed by the respondents despite obtaining
opportunity to file the same. We have independently considered the
averments made in the Applications for condonation of delay and, being
satisfied with the reasons furnished for the delay, allow the Applications
for condonation of delay.
2. Appellants in these appeals filed four writ petitions. The
contentions in those writ petitions were identical. With the consent of the
appellants, those four writ petitions were, accordingly, heard together by a
learned Single Judge of this Court, who, after hearing the same, for the
reasons recorded in the judgment and order under appeals, has dismissed
all those writ petitions and, hence, these appeals.
3. There appears to be no dispute that certain vacancies were
advertised. There is also no dispute that the University, which was
appointed as the selector, considered the merits of the candidates, who
responded to the advertisement, and, thereupon, made recommendations.
There is no dispute that the recommendations were for all the advertised
posts. Accordingly, candidates, who were thus recommended, were given
appointment letters. Some of them, despite having been so appointed, did
not accept the appointments offered to them by the appointment letters.
The University, while making the recommendations, added names of few
candidates to the tune of 25 per cent of the advertised posts and held out
that, after the last recommended candidate, those persons stand
chronologically on the basis of their merit adjudged. Inasmuch as those
people, who had been offered appointments but did not accept the same,
did not supply the advertised vacancies; the appointing authority
approached the State Government seeking permission to fill-up the
advertised posts from amongst those persons listed below the
recommendees in the list prepared by the University, as referred to above.
The State Government refused to accede to the said request. The

3
appointing authority has not shown any grievance in relation thereto.
Instead, those persons, who were listed below the recommendees, filed
the writ petitions and, now, the present appeals.
4. The fact remains that the writ court can uphold fundamental or
otherwise legal rights of a citizen approaching the court. It cannot create
a new right in favour of the person approaching. Admittedly, Rules have
not been framed. Accordingly, there is no direction for preparation of a
wait list. Preparation of the wait list, in the circumstances, is beyond
competence. A person in such a wait list has acquired no right of any
nature, which is enforceable through a mandate of the writ court.
5. That being the situation, there is no scope of interference. The
appeals fail and the same are dismissed.
